one_liner: Rust exact global DNA aligner using A*-guided band doubling over SIMD bit-parallel blocks; beats Edlib and BiWFA on long, similar sequences.
what_it_does: A*PA2 computes the optimal unit-cost edit distance and a CIGAR for global alignment of two DNA sequences. The Rust API is astarpa2_simple(a, b) or astarpa2_full(a, b) in the astarpa2 crate, both returning (Cost, Cigar), with AstarPa2Params for tuning; it is used as a git dependency. A C header (astarpa-c) exposes the same two functions and returns a CIGAR that must be released with astarpa_free_cigar. A pa-bin CLI aligns consecutive pairs from FASTA, .seq or .txt files. It is not an Edlib-compatible API: there are no semi-global or infix modes and no arbitrary alphabets.
how_it_is_fast: Like Edlib, it uses Ukkonen band doubling over Myers' bit-parallel DP, with several changes. It computes 256-column blocks of 64-bit words with std::simd (4 x u64 lanes, two vectors in flight for instruction-level parallelism) and uses a bit-sliced profile that matches a character in two XOR/AND operations. Doubling starts at the heuristic value h(0,0) rather than 0, and each block's row range is narrowed with an admissible A* heuristic: the gap-cost heuristic in -simple, and in -full the gap-chaining seed heuristic (k=12) with match pruning and incremental doubling. Traceback runs diagonal transition over the stored block fronts. On low-divergence pairs the heuristic skips most of the band, so the gain grows with length and shrinks as divergence rises. This is an algorithmic advantage, not a language one.
when_to_use: Exact (optimal) global edit-distance alignment of long DNA pairs, from tens of kbp to Mbp, at low to moderate divergence: for example ONT or PacBio reads, or assembled sequences that should be similar end to end.
When you need a guaranteed-optimal cost and CIGAR, not the heuristic answer of a banded or X-drop aligner, and Edlib or BiWFA are too slow at your lengths.
Rust pipelines that can take a git dependency on a nightly toolchain, or C/C++ code that can link the astarpa-c shared library.
Throughput-bound batches of long pairs on one core per pair; pa-bench measures it single-threaded and pinned to a core, so parallelise across pairs.
when_not_to_use: Short, highly divergent reads: the WABI 2024 abstract (search snippet only) reports 0.81x, i.e. slower than the best of Edlib and BiWFA, on 800 bp ONT reads at 11% divergence.

Any input that is not upper-case A, C, G or T. The profile uses rust-bio's RankTransform over b"ACGT", which panics with 'Unexpected character.' on N, IUPAC codes or lower case: issue #31 ('N characters are not currently supported with A*'), and issue #33 (lower-case bases) is still open. Protein is not supported. Edlib takes arbitrary byte alphabets.
Affine gaps, local or semi-global alignment, or pattern search: it computes global unit-cost edit distance only. Use Sassy or Edlib's infix mode for search.

Builds that must use stable Rust: it needs nightly (rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly-2026-05-21) for portable_simd and the incomplete generic_const_exprs feature, and new nightlies have repeatedly broken the build (issues #28, #32, #36, #41).
Projects that need a versioned package: there is no crates.io release (the README says to add it as a git dependency), and the code is research code with open cleanup issues (#22-#27).

integration.form: crate (git dependency) plus a C API (astarpa-c shared library) and the pa-bin CLI
integration.dependencies: workspace crates pa-types, pa-heuristic, pa-bitpacking, pa-affine-types and pa-vis, plus rust-bio 1.3.0, itertools, clap and serde; SDL2 only for the optional visualizer
integration.min_toolchain: Rust nightly (pinned nightly-2026-05-21, edition 2024; std::simd portable_simd, generic_const_exprs)
integration.platforms: any target std::simd supports; tuned for 256-bit vectors (4 x u64 lanes); the repo's .cargo/config.toml builds with -C target-cpu=native
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each alignment runs single-threaded in its own aligner instance
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same task as Edlib's global (NW) mode with a cost and CIGAR, but a different API, DNA (ACGT) only, and no semi-global or infix modes

gotchas: Input validation is a panic: any byte outside A, C, G and T aborts the alignment with 'Unexpected character.' from rust-bio (issue #31, a pa-bin run on a FASTA file containing N). Sanitise or split on N before calling, and never pass lower-case sequence (issue #33 is open).

Evidence caveats: the numbers that could be opened are the pa-bench notebook means of 7.48x and 8.26x over Edlib. These are arithmetic means of per-(length, error-rate) runtime ratios on uniform-random synthetic pairs, so they are weighted toward the largest-n cells. They use capped runtimes: a timeout counts as the time limit, any other failure as 1.1x the limit, and a failure skips all larger jobs. The 19x, 5.6x and 0.81x paper figures were seen only in search snippets, since dagstuhl and bioRxiv are blocked here, and no CPU model is stated anywhere.

Build flags of the published runs are undocumented: pa-bench has no .cargo/config.toml and its justfile sets no RUSTFLAGS, so the aligner repo's target-cpu=native does not apply when pa-bench builds A*PA2 as a git dependency. Edlib is built through edlib-rs and the cmake crate, whose '-D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release' is passed as a C flag, not a CMake option. pa-bench does cross-check costs between exact aligners and validates every CIGAR, so no correctness flaw was found behind the numbers.

The -full variant builds a k-mer seed heuristic (k=12, pruning) before aligning. Issues #29 and #30 were block-indexing and traceback panics, both closed in September 2024, so pin a known-good commit (pa-bench's Cargo.lock uses f83c131).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick A*PA2 for exact end-to-end alignment of long, similar DNA sequences. Pick Sassy (same author) to find short patterns with errors inside long texts, and bitdp for batched throughput on many short (150 bp to 1 kbp) pairs, where bitdp beats Edlib and A*PA2's long-read advantage does not apply.
verified_claims_summary: Opened first-party evidence: the pa-bench evals notebook reports A*PA2-simple averaging 7.48x (scaling-n) and 8.26x (scaling-e) faster than Edlib (C++, through edlib-rs) on synthetic pairs. scaling-n runs 3 kbp to 10 Mbp at 5% and 15% uniform error with traceback, a 3 h and 32 GiB limit, one pinned core at a fixed 3.6 GHz, and no CPU model given. The WABI 2024 paper reports 19x on >500 kbp ONT reads at 6% divergence, 5.6x at 11 kbp and 11%, and 0.81x at 800 bp and 11% against the best of Edlib and BiWFA (C), but these were seen only in search snippets.
status_note: Active research code (last commit 2026-05-22, nightly-toolchain fixes) under MPL-2.0, a file-level copyleft that permits linking. It is usable as a git dependency or C shared library, but only for upper-case ACGT input and only with a nightly toolchain.
